Prepare a multiome object for layered network inference

Source: R/find_motifs.R
prepare_candidates.Rd

Builds the candidate catalogue used by fit_layered_network: it initializes the multiCSN state without marker filtering (every RNA gene is a candidate target), aligns the gene annotation with the peak chromosome names and scans the selected peaks for motifs.

Usage

prepare_candidates(
  object,
  group.by = "aggregate",
  genome,
  rna_assay = "RNA",
  peak_assay = "ATAC",
  targets = NULL,
  pfm = NULL,
  motif_tfs = NULL,
  backend = c("motifmatchr", "signac"),
  exclude_exons = TRUE,
  align_annotation = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object with normalized RNA and TF-IDF chromatin assays.

group.by

Metadata column with the cell groups to fit, or "aggregate" for one group with all cells.

genome

A BSgenome object matching the peak coordinates.

rna_assay, peak_assay

Assay names.

targets

Candidate target genes; defaults to every RNA gene.

pfm, motif_tfs

Motif matrices and motif-to-TF map; default to the bundled motifs and motif2tf.

backend

Motif scanning backend, see find_motifs.

exclude_exons

Remove exonic peaks from the candidates.

align_annotation

Add peak chromosomes missing from the gene annotation to its sequence levels.

verbose

Print progress messages.

Value

The object with candidate genes, peaks, transcription factors and motif matches.

Details

Both assays require a single normalized layer named data. Join split layers with SeuratObject::JoinLayers() before preparing candidates. RNA values must use the normalization intended for the fit; chromatin values must be TF-IDF normalized. This function does not normalize either assay.

Every call rebuilds the multiCSN candidate catalogue and clears networks from the previous catalogue on the returned object. It sets active identities from group.by, selects the RNA default assay and, when requested, extends annotation sequence levels. Other assays and metadata are retained. Keep the returned object and reuse it for fits of the same catalogue.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
genome <- BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38::BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38
object <- prepare_candidates(object, group.by = "cell_type", genome = genome)
fit <- fit_layered_network(object, cell_group = "HSC", preset = "state")
} # }
